interpretation: The reported 9.8547 W whole-capture average and sustained idle-loop pattern reproduce the earlier high-drain symptom despite unchanged recorded kernel/driver inputs.
The initial long freeze does not itself measure power, but distinguishes a transition within this suspend from an idle loop present immediately at entry.
No full desktop resume occurred when the internal pattern changed. The trace does not identify the initiating firmware or CPU-idle return reason.
A reboot is not a guaranteed remedy: this was the first recorded suspend in a different boot from the earlier good sequence.
Most half-second exits lack corresponding handled Linux interrupts; the intermittent arch_timer/IPI events do not establish a cause for every exit.
limitations: Power is for the whole 1195.66-second capture, including 80 seconds outside suspend.
No energy sample at the 325-second transition exists, so separate pre/post-transition power cannot be calculated.
Endpoint temperatures do not establish continuous thermal history.
Software successful-suspend counters do not establish efficient hardware low-power residency.
next_step: Preserve the current boot state; investigate CPU-idle and PSCI entry/return values around the transition rather than treating another reboot as a fix. Any additional tracing must be validated before the next manually performed lid test.
